note:
rollup() now uses ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=min(attached_projects, 16)) with a module-level _project_row() worker; rows/totals stay in registration order via pool.map, unattached rows never reach a worker (no Store built), per-project exceptions still become "error:" rows, and a hub with nothing attached skips the pool (no max_workers=0). 189 hub tests pass; parity vs the old sequential implementation verified byte-for-byte on a 6-attached + 2-unattached hub, deterministic over 8 runs.

BLOCKER on the perf DoD: threads make rollup SLOWER, not faster. rollup's per-project work is in-process markdown/YAML parsing, which holds the GIL - unlike git_status_all, whose speedup comes from subprocesses. Measured (warm page cache, best of 5, caches cleared per run): 6 projects x 60 stories 72ms sequential vs 151ms threaded (0.48x); 12 projects x 60 stories 121ms vs 266ms (0.45x). Raw file reads are only 10.7ms of 130ms total (8%), so there is almost no blocking I/O for threads to overlap. ProcessPoolExecutor on the same 12-project fixture: 143ms -> 62ms including pool startup (2.3x faster). So "uses ThreadPoolExecutor" and "performance improvement measurable on 5+ project hubs" are in conflict; the code as directed satisfies the first and fails the second. Needs a product/design call: switch to ProcessPoolExecutor, drop the perf criterion, or attack the cost in build_index instead. Sibling test task US-PRJ-34-4 (perf test) will fail as specified.
